l1_posteriors.label: Cutaneous Metastasis from Solid Organ Malignancy

A.rationale: Cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma is a broader term that encompasses the specific diagnosis

B.rationale: Carcinoma erysipeloides is a variant of cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma

C.rationale: Telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma is a specific diagnosis that matches the leaf labels

D.rationale: Carcinoma en cuirasse is a sclerodermiform variant of breast carcinoma metastasis, which is a subtype of cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma

vignette_preview:
A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face. Medical history includes left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier, treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy. Seven years after initial diagnosis, she had left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision. Current symptoms include pain on palpation, with no fever or chills.

Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face.

- Histopathological examination:  Findings: Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis. One vessel showed nests of highly atypical cells.    - Immunohistochemical examination:  Results: Epithelial cells in the dilated vessels were positive for CD31, and the atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3.    - Images:  Figure 1 Title: Full and three-quarters image of the face  Figure 1 Description: Telangiectatic, swelling erythema mainly involving the left side of the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek    Figure 2 Title: Histopathological and immunohistochemical images  Figure 2A Description: H
